svg.title: Hydrogen tunnelling in Fe: one proton, two sites
svg.text: Hydrogen tunnelling in Fe: one proton, two sites
Classically the proton would stay in one well. Quantum mechanically it leaks through the barrier and back.

Tunnel splitting 215 µeV: one pass from well to well takes 9.62 ps.
Deuterium, twice as heavy, in the same wells: splitting 9.24 µeV, one pass takes 224 ps.
Model: barrier height and width from the table; harmonic wells at the attempt frequency (1e+13 Hz); exact 1D states on a grid.
